items.title: Arini Capital Management ($7.0bn AUM) $800m forced liquid debt liquidation on prime-brokerage margin calls (~26% YTD drawdown)
items.query: Arini Capital Management 800m forced debt sale margin calls October 2026 PIMCO Oaktree Altice Optimum Virgin Media
items.excerpt: London-based credit hedge fund Arini Capital Management (~$7.0bn AUM, founded by Hamza Lemssouguer) was forced to offload roughly $800m of more-liquid corporate loans and high-yield bonds into month-end October 2026 to meet prime-brokerage margin calls and bolster cash buffers after flagship fund YTD losses deepened from >20% mid-October to ~26% by 30 October 2026. Losses were concentrated in illiquid, high-conviction distressed telecom and cyclical bets including Altice International, Optimum Communications (formerly Altice USA), Virgin Media, Brightspeed, Aston Martin, and Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection, with PIMCO and Oaktree emerging as opportunistic buyers of the discounted BWIC blocks.

items.title: European CLO YTD volume (€94.9bn / 229 deals), late-Oct 126–129 bps AAA prints, Single-B 880–1,015 bps dispersion, and Solvency II Jan 2027 tailwind
items.query: European CLO October 2026 issuance AAA Single-B 880 1015 bps BofA 60bn Solvency II January 2027 Creditflux Trepp
items.excerpt: European CLO issuance reached €94.9bn across 229 deals through September 2026 (September printed €10.7bn across 24 deals: €7.6bn new issue across 17 deals at 124 bps AAA and €3.1bn refi/resets across 7 deals at 120 bps AAA, a 4 bps refi/reset discount). Entering November 2026 with >100 open European warehouses and Bank of America projecting ~€60bn of FY26 refi/reset volume ahead of January 2027 EU Solvency II securitisation capital-charge relief, late-October European new-issue AAA cleared at 126–129 bps while primary Single-B tranches exhibited extreme manager dispersion from 880 bps to 1,015 bps against 12–16% annualised CLO equity cash-on-cash distributions.

items.title: Fitch European CLO 'triple squeeze' (~350 bps WAS, 10 bps cushion, 10% tail) & US BSL CLO AAA–BB 381.5 bps basis and post-RP 2.1% Jr OC
items.query: Fitch European CLO WAS 350 bps 10 bps cushion triple squeeze US BSL CLO BB 500 bps Junior OC 2.1% October 2026
items.excerpt: Fitch European CLO surveillance shows average portfolio Weighted Average Spread (WAS) compressed 36 bps below its 10-year average to ~350 bps, leaving average WAS cushion at ~10 bps alongside ~0.9 pt WARF and ~3.9% WARR cushions, with 10% of low-WAS European CLOs trapped in a 'triple squeeze' driving junior 'F'-note downgrades. In the US ($41.1bn YTD BSL issuance across 92 deals; September $4.4bn across 9 deals), tier-1 AAA held at 118–119 bps while primary BB widened +60 bps in October to ~500 bps (a 381.5 bps AAA–BB basis), reflecting Fitch's bifurcation between reinvesting US BSL CLOs (9.3% Senior OC / 4.5% Junior OC at WARF 2835) and post-reinvestment deals (>68% Senior OC vs just 2.1% Junior OC cushion).

items.title: Optimum Communications ($26.0bn CSC Holdings debt) pre-arranged Chapter 11 equitization — Drahi abandons $3.0bn stake ask as Apollo, Oaktree & JPMorgan take control
items.query: Optimum Communications Altice USA CSC Holdings 26 billion pre-arranged Chapter 11 Drahi 3 billion Apollo Oaktree JPMorgan October 2026
items.excerpt: Weekend restructuring wires report Patrick Drahi is abandoning his prior demand to retain roughly $3.0bn of post-reorganisation equity in Optimum Communications (formerly Altice USA / CSC Holdings LLC, carrying ~$26.0bn of consolidated debt) ahead of an expected pre-arranged Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing that will hand majority equity control to first-lien creditors led by Apollo Global Management, Oaktree Capital Management, and JPMorgan after antitrust litigation fractured out-of-court LME cooperation arrangements.

items.title: Altice International (~$9.0bn / ~€8.0bn debt) NY Commercial Division lawsuit, end-of-October NDA cliff, and Arini steering-plaintiff liquidity stress
items.query: Altice International NY Supreme Court Commercial Division lawsuit 1.5bn Arini Invesco Sona Diameter Elliott NDA October 2026
items.excerpt: Altice International (~$9.0bn / ~€8.0bn total debt, ~€3.1bn 2027 maturity wall, ~€528m cash and undrawn RCF vs ~€346m LTM negative FCF) faces end-of-October 2026 NDA expiry deadlines alongside the 13 October 2026 NY Supreme Court Commercial Division lawsuit filed by a five-manager steering committee (Arini, Invesco, Sona, Diameter, and Elliott, holding >$1.5bn of term loans plus senior secured notes inside a ~90% co-op renewed through March 2027) challenging the November 2025 €750m 12% Portugal/Caribbean unrestricted drop-down. Arini's ~26% YTD drawdown and $800m forced liquidation inject acute secondary-supply and negotiating-cohesion risk directly into the Altice International steering group.

items.title: Virgin Media O2 (~£22.0bn debt/leases, B+ >6.1x leverage) mass-redundancy cost overhaul under UK CMA fiber block & VodafoneZiggo 86.0 pts TLB mark
items.query: Virgin Media O2 redundancies cost cutting UK CMA nexfibre Netomnia 22bn VodafoneZiggo 86 October 2026
items.excerpt: Following Fitch's downgrade of Virgin Media O2 (~£22.0bn debt and lease stack, >6.1x net leverage) to B+ (aligning with S&P B+ Negative) and the UK Competition and Markets Authority's refusal to grant fast-track clearance to nexfibre's £2.0bn Netomnia acquisition (stalling ~£1.0bn of projected VMO2 cash-deleveraging proceeds), VMO2 prepared sweeping operational cost cuts and workforce redundancies at month-end October 2026 to defend 2027 cash flows, while sister Liberty Global JV VodafoneZiggo's €1.125bn Term Loan B due 2033 remained depressed near 86.0 pts after a 6.7 pts multi-strategy pod sell-off.

items.title: Thames Water downgraded by S&P to CCC- (27 Oct 2026) after 16 Oct Class B TSA, £5.4bn super-senior priming upsize, and £10.0bn L&VW RP2 proposal
items.query: Thames Water S&P downgrade CCC- October 2026 Class B TSA 5.4bn super senior London Valley Water 10bn RP2 Ofwat
items.excerpt: On 27 October 2026, S&P Global Ratings downgraded Thames Water (~£16.0bn WBS debt; ~£20.0bn total group debt) to CCC-, citing near-inevitable default/haircut execution within six months following the binding 16 October 2026 Class B Transaction Support Agreement (>60% of ~£1.0bn Class B written off for ~5.9% post-restructured equity plus £150m equity rights). Thames Water has drawn £2.65bn of its £3.0bn super-senior rescue facility and is seeking a £2.4bn upsize to £5.4bn past the March 2027 Stable Platform expiry, while senior Class A consortium London & Valley Water (Elliott, Silver Point; Akin Gump, Jefferies) awaits formal Ofwat acceptance of its ~£10.0bn Restructuring Plan 2 (RP2).

items.title: Fitch cuts France (A+) outlook to Negative (30 Oct 2026) as Fitch European loan TTM defaults jump +90 bps to 3.6% on French LBOs (Cerba, Arxada) and US loan defaults hit 3.9%
items.query: Fitch France A+ Negative outlook October 30 2026 Fitch European leveraged loan default rate 3.6% Cerba Arxada US 3.9%
items.excerpt: In an unscheduled review on 30 October 2026, Fitch Ratings cut France's (A+) sovereign outlook to Negative from Stable on fiscal gridlock (5.4%–5.5% 2026 deficit, public debt rising from 115.7% to 124.0% of GDP by 2028, Q3 GDP contraction, 0.5% 2026 growth, and 10Y OAT yields near 5.0%). Concurrently, Fitch's October 2026 default monitor reported the European leveraged loan TTM default rate jumped +90 bps MoM from 2.7% to 3.6% (4.0%–4.5% YE26 forecast; EUR HY defaults up to 2.6%), led explicitly by French LBO restructurings including Cerba Healthcare and Arxada alongside Victoria. In the US, Fitch's institutional loan TTM default rate rose to 3.9% ($7.0bn September volume across 9 distressed debt exchanges and 2 Chapter 11 filings), with Top Market Concern loans at 7.8% (>10.3% combined watch list), >55% of defaults structured as LMEs, and ~55% of LME issuers re-defaulting within 18–24 months.

items.excerpt: Across the $2.9tn global AI data-centre buildout (~$1.5tn external debt gap through 2028; $30–40bn projected annual data-centre ABS/CMBS issuance alongside Moody's warning on circular vendor-borrower SPVs), late-October 2026 capital markets enforced sharp credit rationing: (1) S&P revised Meta Platforms' (AA-) outlook to Negative as AI CapEx scaled toward $140bn in 2026 and >$225bn in 2027, flipping Meta toward negative free cash flow and heavier bond issuance; (2) OpenAI cut its equity raise target by $10bn from $30bn to $20bn (at a $1.25tn valuation) after securing <50% of commitments; (3) Blackstone warned Anthropic is likely to receive a speculative-grade BB ('high junk') credit rating post-IPO despite Project North Star chip-collateralised debt; (4) Amazon reported -$42bn of trailing 12-month FCF burn against a $578bn AWS backlog; and (5) Intel plunged -28.58% after guiding zero 2027 FCF ($600m Fab 28 outage) and warning of 5x DRAM/NAND memory inflation squeezing working-capital credit lines across server/PC OEMs Dell (-10.82%), HP (-8.90%), HPE (-6.68%), and Super Micro (-6.62%).
